main_text.head: SECT. X. De Satisfactionibus.
main_text.p: AFfinis est merito satisfactio : & reuera quasi furculus quidam, ex eadem radice suppullulat : quâ nihil vnquam fingi potuit in Christi merita contumeliosius : Nec displicuit patribus vocabulum, nec illorum sensu, nobis. Illud modo fas monuisse ; Incautas Tert. de praescript. αντιχρηστους vocum, magno Ecclesiae malo, rerum induxisse confusionem ; vti contrà (verè Tertullianus) Fides nominum salus proprietatum: Nihil nobis istic cum ciuili sa-tis-

page.notes: The first word "AFfinis" is a large initial A joined to "ffinis" (read as Affinis). The Greek word after "Incautas" is rendered in transliteration in the printed form and is hard to read; it is marked as printed in Greek letters as best read. The margin note reads "Tert. de praescript." in italic. The word "satisfactio" is printed "satisfa-ctio" across a line break. Show-through text from the reverse page (upper right) is excluded.
